title: Practice forgiveness until fear loosens
summary: Forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment are named as the true fast. The practice weakens the inner sickness that keeps death-fear near.
takeaway: Keep the fast of forgiveness before resentment feeds again.
lifeApplication: When resentment asks for another rehearsal, withhold the sentence that keeps it alive. Let restraint, conduct, and contentment become the fast you actually keep.

source.shortMeaning: Forgiveness, conduct, and contentment form a fast that frees the heart from affliction and death-fear.
source.lifeApplication: When resentment rises, drop one sentence you keep feeding and let contentment answer first.

evidence.coreClaim: Forgiveness, conduct, and contentment form a fast that frees the heart from affliction and death-fear.
evidence.turn: The shabad treats forgiveness not as a mood but as disciplined abstinence from resentment.
evidence.practicalImplication: When resentment asks for another rehearsal, withhold the sentence that keeps it alive. Let restraint, conduct, and contentment become the fast you actually keep.
